title.narrative: Supporting the Development of Voluntary Local Reviews (VLRs) in BiH and Georgia through Experience Exchange with Other VLR Cities in the Eastern Europe and Central Asian Region

description.narrative:
This project, funded under the Joint SDG Fund’s SDG Localization window, seeks to increase multiple institutional capabilities and involvement in SDG localization in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) and Georgia’s selected municipalities by supporting the development of Action-Oriented Voluntary Local Reviews (VLRs). VLRs are important tools for local monitoring and supporting the localization of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The initiative is led by FAO in BiH and UNDP in Georgia, with technical support from UN-Habitat.
APPROACH: The project uses a multi-stakeholder approach as well as builds capacity to support effective localization, all to help incorporate Sustainable Development Goals and food systems into multiple voluntary local reviews. Key strategies include:
Capacity building importantly improves the knowledge in addition to the skills of local authorities and stakeholders. They can then more effectively monitor as well as report on SDG progress.
To substantially increase cooperation, local, national and international groups can work together at multiple levels with outfits like FAO, UNDP, WHO, UNICEF and UN-Habitat.
The Twinning Program sets up multiple partnerships for knowledge sharing between municipalities in both BiH and Georgia and one municipality in the EU that provides for them.
To guarantee a consistent methodology and the incorporation of agrifood systems in SDG reporting, methodological support is available from UN-Habitat, thanks to their expertise in VLR development.
MAIN EXPECTED ACCOMPLISHMENTS: 1. Strengthened Institutional Capacities: Enhanced engagement of local authorities in BiH (Trebinje, Bijeljina, Kakanj, and Siroki Brijeg) and Georgia (Khashuri and Poti) in SDG localization and monitoring. 2. Technical Support to the development of the Action-Oriented VLRs: Facilitating evidence-based decision-making and policy planning through structured sub-national reviews. 3. Regional and International Knowledge Exchange: Supporting peer learning and best practice dissemination via the twinning programme with an EU provider municipality.
